title: What If Humans Had Wings? Could We Fly?

scenes.text: What if humans had wings? Growing them is the easy part. Flying is the problem.
To lift an adult, the wings would need to span at least 22 feet, about 6.7 meters.
Flapping them takes chest muscles roughly twice the size of a pro bodybuilder's.
Your skeleton would need a keel on the chest and a fused wishbone, like a bird's, to anchor them.
Birds also have one-way airflow in their lungs and faster reflexes. We have neither.
So the best you'd manage is gliding, like the giant extinct bird Argentavis, with its twenty-foot wings.

description:
What if humans had wings?
Wingspan of about 22 feet, chest muscles twice a bodybuilder's, and a bird-style keel, and you still might only glide.
